items.title: Ancient DNA reveals how plague kept returning for 400 years after the Black Death
items.summary: Ancient DNA reveals that plague repeatedly returned to Europe for more than 400 years after the Black Death, evolving into new lineages and spreading through trade, migration, and war. items.title: Part-human part-mouse brain developed in science breakthrough
items.summary: Researchers at Stanford University genetically altered mice to be able to receive and function with human brain cells.

items.title: Scientists opened a sealed envelope after 10 years. Gravity still didn’t make sense
items.summary: A decade-long NIST experiment has produced a new measurement of the universal gravitational constant that differs unexpectedly from another leading result, deepening a 225-year-old physics puzzle. items.title: A 66-million-year-old tooth reveals T. rex was nearly as warm as a human
items.summary: Chemical clues preserved inside fossilized T. rex teeth reveal that the dinosaur maintained a body temperature of about 97 degrees Fahrenheit, almost identical to humans. The finding provides direct evidence that the giant predator was warm-blooded, helping explain how it stayed active and survived

items.title: Scientists may have solved a 2,000-year-old Dead Sea Scrolls mystery
items.summary: Researchers may have solved a long-running mystery surrounding the Dead Sea Scrolls by proposing that the Qumran sect really did use its distinctive 364-day calendar.
